title: Checks for the use of extraneous whitespace after "(", "[" or "{".
summary: PEP 8 recommends the omission of whitespace in the following cases: - "Immediately inside parentheses, brackets or braces." - "Immediately before a comma, semicolon, or colon." Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for the use of extraneous whitespace before ")", "]" or "}".
summary: PEP 8 recommends the omission of whitespace in the following cases: - "Immediately inside parentheses, brackets or braces." - "Immediately before a comma, semicolon, or colon." Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for the use of extraneous whitespace before ",", ";" or ":".
summary: PEP 8 recommends the omission of whitespace in the following cases: - "Immediately inside parentheses, brackets or braces." - "Immediately before a comma, semicolon, or colon." Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for trailing whitespace after a decorator's opening @.
summary: Including whitespace after the @ symbol is not compliant with PEP 8. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for extraneous whitespace immediately preceding an open parenthesis or bracket.
summary: According to PEP 8, open parentheses and brackets should not be preceded by any trailing whitespace. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for extraneous whitespace before an operator.
summary: According to PEP 8, operators should be surrounded by at most a single space on either side. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for extraneous whitespace after an operator.
summary: According to PEP 8, operators should be surrounded by at most a single space on either side. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for extraneous tabs before an operator.
summary: According to PEP 8, operators should be surrounded by at most a single space on either side. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for extraneous tabs after an operator.
summary: According to PEP 8, operators should be surrounded by at most a single space on either side. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for missing whitespace around all operators.
summary: According to PEP 8, there should be one space before and after all assignment (=), augmented assignment (+=, -=, etc.), comparison, and Booleans operators. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for missing whitespace arithmetic operators.
summary: PEP 8 recommends never using more than one space, and always having the same amount of whitespace on both sides of a binary operator. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for missing whitespace around bitwise and shift operators.
summary: PEP 8 recommends never using more than one space, and always having the same amount of whitespace on both sides of a binary operator. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.
message_templates: Missing whitespace around bitwise or shift operator

title: Checks for missing whitespace around the modulo operator.
summary: PEP 8 recommends never using more than one space, and always having the same amount of whitespace on both sides of a binary operator. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for missing whitespace after ,, ;, and :.
summary: Missing whitespace after ,, ;, and : makes the code harder to read. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for extraneous whitespace after a comma.
summary: Consistency is good. This rule helps ensure you have a consistent formatting style across your project. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for extraneous tabs after a comma.
summary: Commas should be followed by one space, never tabs. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: UTF-16 and UTF-32 aren't backward compatible. Use UTF-8 instead.
summary: For compatibility use UTF-8 instead of UTF-16/UTF-32. See also https://bugs.python.org/issue1503789 for a history of this issue. And https://softwareengineering.stackexchange.com/questions/102205/ for some possible problems when using UTF-16 for instance. pylint calls it invalid-unicode-codec.
message_templates: UTF-16 and UTF-32 aren't backward compatible. Use UTF-8 instead

title: Contains control characters that can permit obfuscated code executed differently than displayed.
summary: Bidirectional unicode are typically not displayed characters required to display right-to-left (RTL) script (i.e. Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Hebrew, ...) correctly. So can you trust this code? Are you sure it displayed correctly in all editors? If you did not write it or your language is not RTL, remove the special characters, as they could be used to trick you into executing code, that does something else than what it looks like. More Information: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bidirectional_text https://trojansource.codes/. pylint calls it bidirectional-unicode.
message_templates: Contains control characters that can permit obfuscated code executed differently than displayed

title: Checks for missing whitespace around the equals sign in an unannotated function keyword parameter.
summary: According to PEP 8, there should be no spaces around the equals sign in a keyword parameter, if it is unannotated: Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.
message_templates: Unexpected spaces around keyword / parameter equals

title: Invalid unescaped character backspace, use "b" instead.
summary: Moves the cursor back, so the character after it will overwrite the character before. pylint calls it invalid-character-backspace.
message_templates: Invalid unescaped character backspace, use "b" instead.

title: Invalid unescaped character carriage-return, use "r" instead.
summary: Moves the cursor to the start of line, subsequent characters overwrite the start of the line. pylint calls it invalid-character-carriage-return.
message_templates: Invalid unescaped character carriage-return, use "r" instead.

title: Invalid unescaped character sub, use "x1A" instead.
summary: Ctrl+Z "End of text" on Windows. Some programs (such as type) ignore the rest of the file after it. pylint calls it invalid-character-sub.
message_templates: Invalid unescaped character sub, use "x1A" instead.

title: Invalid unescaped character esc, use "x1B" instead.
summary: Commonly initiates escape codes which allow arbitrary control of the terminal. pylint calls it invalid-character-esc.
message_templates: Invalid unescaped character esc, use "x1B" instead.

title: Invalid unescaped character nul, use "0" instead.
summary: Mostly end of input for python. pylint calls it invalid-character-nul.
message_templates: Invalid unescaped character nul, use "0" instead.

title: Invalid unescaped character zero-width-space, use "u200B" instead.
summary: Invisible space character could hide real code execution. pylint calls it invalid-character-zero-width-space.
message_templates: Invalid unescaped character zero-width-space, use "u200B" instead.

title: Checks for missing whitespace around the equals sign in an annotated function keyword parameter.
summary: According to PEP 8, the spaces around the equals sign in a keyword parameter should only be omitted when the parameter is unannotated: Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks if inline comments are separated by at least two spaces.
summary: An inline comment is a comment on the same line as a statement. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks if one space is used after inline comments.
summary: An inline comment is a comment on the same line as a statement. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for block comments that lack a single space after the leading # character.
summary: Per PEP 8, "Block comments generally consist of one or more paragraphs built out of complete sentences, with each sentence ending in a period." Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for block comments that start with multiple leading # characters.
